name: stock_footage_commercial
summary: A fast-paced editing breakdown video demonstrating how to produce a million-dollar commercial on a low budget using asset packs and stock footage. It is characterized by frequent punch-ins on talking heads, hand-drawn paper sketch overlays, animated brush text, and rhythmic montage cutting.

captions.notes: Crisp white sans-serif subtitles with a subtle drop shadow displayed in short natural phrases during skits and narrative beats.

headline.notes: Large handwritten or brush-stroke titles rendered over textured film-burn or crumpled paper slates.

callouts.notes: Hand-drawn chalk/pencil doodles on crumpled paper backgrounds combined with giant yellow pop-in dollar amounts.

transitions.notes: Jump-cut punch-ins for talking head emphasis; stylized film grit, light leaks, and kinetic whip transitions for montage sequences.

rules: Punch in on the A-roll speaker every few seconds to reset visual interest.
Introduce budget constraints and key figures with oversized yellow pop-in text.
Cut rapid montages on musical downbeats and percussive transients.
Use stop-motion crumpled paper sketches to visualize conceptual workflows.
Layer neon glow strokes or graphic wraps over footage to unify mismatched stock clips.
Frame timeline tutorials with an over-the-shoulder picture-in-picture webcam.
Bookend commercial sequences with matching master shots to create narrative closure.
avoid: Static wide talking-head shots lasting longer than 4 seconds.
Stock corporate lower-thirds or sterile corporate motion graphics.
Dead air or pauses between spoken dialogue.
Overly clinical color grading without added texture or film overlays.
